## We begin this semester amid significant change

### Illinois Tech's transformation

- Painful departures of colleagues, mentors, and friends who have shaped this community; we [grieve]{.alert}

- New academic structures, [no departments]{.alert}

- Questions and uncertainty; let's meet them with patience and care

- We remain committed to your [success]{.alert}

::: {.key-point style="margin-top: -0.4em;"}
The loss is real, as is our responsibility to care for one another and
keep learning well
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources]

- Elizabeth Hudson and Jeff Wereszczynski, “How to Talk with Students About
  the Academic Transformation FAQ Resources,” email to faculty and staff,
  August 7, 2026
- Illinois Tech, “Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ),” Academic Transformation
  SharePoint hub, accessed August 13, 2026
:::

## The new structure connects depth, disciplines, and practice

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}

- [Depth]{.alert} in a chosen field remains essential
- Consequential problems [cross]{.alert} traditional academic boundaries
- Interdisciplinary pathways should be [easier]{.alert} to find and pursue
- Research, applied learning, and career preparation should [connect]{.alert}
  more directly

:::

## Further significant changes

### The advance of AI

AI can be a capable assistant that helps [solve]{.alert} research problems

- [Ken Ono: How AI Will Unleash a New Kind of Intelligence](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jGZOi-7haCw&t=23s)
- [Terence Tao: Mathematics in the Age of AI](https://teorth.github.io/tao-web/slides/age-of-ai-icm-2026.pdf)
- [Leiden Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Mathematics](https://leidendeclaration.ai/)
- [The Washington Post: Mathematicians ask what’s left for humans when AI can do math research](https://www.washingtonpost.com/technology/2026/08/19/mathematicians-ask-whats-left-humans-when-ai-can-do-math-research/)

::: {.key-point style="margin-top: -0.4em;"}
We need to understand what AI produces—and learn how to guide it
:::
